clue.text: Tax cut

explanation.surface: A two-word note about a reduction in taxation.
explanation.definitionFit: An excise is a duty levied on goods, and to excise is to remove surgically or edit out.

clue.text: You're probably surprised when they go up

definitions.text: You're probably surprised when they go up

parts.words: You're probably surprised when they go up
parts.note: the things rising are the arched hair lines above the eyes, lifted in astonishment

explanation.surface: A remark about something that rises when you feel astonished.
explanation.definitionFit: People raise the hair arches above their eyes in astonishment.

clue.text: What the lost horse-shoe was made of?

definitions.text: What the lost horse-shoe was made of?

parts.words: What the lost horse-shoe was made of?
parts.note: a horse that loses a shoe is said to have cast it, so a shoe moulded from metal is also a shoe that was thrown off

explanation.surface: A question about the material of a horseshoe that went missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast iron is iron shaped in a mould; 'cast' is also what a horse does when it sheds a shoe.

clue.text: Fail to keep up a legend

parts.note: something that fails to keep up droops or sags

explanation.surface: A myth that will not stay standing.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long heroic tale, a legend.

clue.text: A gem you can safely handle

definitions.text: A gem you can safely handle

parts.words: A gem you can safely handle
parts.note: a gem suggests a jewel, but this one is a hand-held firework that throws out glittering points; slang for a diamond

explanation.surface: Advice on a precious stone that poses no risk to hold.
explanation.definitionFit: The hand-held firework is the one kind children are allowed to hold, and slang calls a diamond the same word.

clue.text: Innocent chap in trouble driven to take away furniture

indicators.note: something in trouble is in a mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A blameless man in difficulty is forced to steal tables and chairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driven' looks like 'forced', but it means a vehicle someone drives. 'in trouble' rearranges INNOCENTCHAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantechnicon is a large British removal van used to move household goods.

clue.text: Herb's sure about foreign ways, and is sorry

indicators.note: about means the letters of sure are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener's herb is certain about overseas customs and apologises.
explanation.walkthrough: Several readings meet: RUE'S (the herb's), French rues (streets, 'foreign ways'), RUES (is sorry), and 'about' rearranging SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rue is a bitter herb; rues are French streets; to rue is to regret.

clue.text: Lehar composition about love set in Pakistan

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, around, the zero letter
a composition is something put together, so the letters of Lehar are arranged anew

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: An operetta by Franz Lehar about romance staged in South Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: Franz Lehar wrote The Merry Widow. 'composition' rearranges LEHAR to LAHRE, and 'about' puts it round O.
explanation.definitionFit: Lahore is the capital of Punjab province, a city in Pakistan.

clue.text: Artist given food-a bit of salad

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword stand-in for artist
a dish is a prepared item of food

explanation.surface: A painter is served a meal, including some salad.
explanation.definitionFit: A radish is a crisp root vegetable eaten raw in salads.

clue.text: Officer found on the staff

explanation.surface: A military man discovered among the personnel.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensign is a junior commissioned officer, and also a flag flown from a flagstaff.

clue.text: Coming in last, after me, she gets caught

indicators.note: the pair of words 'me' and 'she' come into the middle of the word for last, splitting it open

parts.note: the last part of something is its end

indicators.note: the word 'she' is placed after the word 'me' in the inserted run

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman finishing last behind the speaker is trapped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming in' and 'after' look like race commentary about finishing last; they are the container and order signals, and 'gets' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be enmeshed is to be tangled in a net, that is trapped or caught.

clue.text: Gives publicity to rows in foreign parts

explanation.surface: A note that quarrels overseas get reported.
explanation.definitionFit: To noise abroad is to spread news widely; noises abroad also reads as rows (din) heard overseas.

clue.text: Attack causing rapid loss of heart

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, and loss of it means the middle letter of rapid is dropped

explanation.surface: An offensive in which the fast pace is suddenly lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loss of heart' removes P, the central letter of RAPID.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden assault or incursion.

clue.text: Shady place for one on the fiddle?

explanation.surface: A cool spot suited to a swindler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the fiddle' suggests cheating, but here it means someone drawing a bow across a violin.
explanation.definitionFit: A bower is a leafy shelter in a garden; a violinist plays with a bow, making a playful noun for that player.

clue.text: Flag of Eire shortened

indicators.note: shortened means the word is cut back by its final letter

parts.note: Eire is Ireland, so something of Eire is Irish

explanation.surface: The Irish national banner cut down in size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' suggests a national banner; it is the plant also called the yellow flag. 'shortened' drops H from IRISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag is a common name for the iris plant, especially the yellow water iris.

clue.text: Lifting of spirit in debate

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting means the word of is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: Raising one's spirits during a discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifting' turns OF into FO; 'in' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is a meeting or medium for open public discussion.

clue.text: Eccentric cheer-leader at head of column

indicators.note: in a down clue, at head of places the first piece on top of the next
the leader of a word is its opening letter, taken from cheer

parts.note: a rank is a line of soldiers, a column in formation

explanation.surface: An odd pompom-waving cheerleader marching at the front of a parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheer-leader' poses as one word but gives C, the first letter of 'cheer'.
explanation.definitionFit: A crank is an odd person with obsessive ideas.

clue.text: Guarded inquiry

parts.note: guarded seems to mean cautious, but it is the challenge called out by a sentry guarding a gate to someone approaching

explanation.surface: A cautious, non-committal question.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry on guard duty calls out this traditional challenge to anyone approaching in the dark.

clue.text: Tubes of paste

parts.note: paste suggests toothpaste or glue in tubes, but it is the Italian word for pasta, made in hollow tubular shapes

explanation.surface: Containers of glue or toothpaste.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni is a dried pasta in short hollow tubes; Italian paste means pasta.

clue.text: Son sleeping should be gamboling

parts.note: kipping is British slang for sleeping

explanation.surface: A boy who is asleep ought to be running about.
explanation.definitionFit: Skipping means bounding lightly, frolicking.

clue.text: It normally completes the written enquiry

definitions.text: It normally completes the written enquiry

parts.words: It normally completes the written enquiry
parts.note: a written query normally ends with a particular punctuation symbol placed after its last word

explanation.surface: Something that usually finishes off a written investigation.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation symbol ? ends a written interrogative sentence.

clue.text: Proceed to make good

explanation.surface: Go ahead and fix things up.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair is to go to a place, as in repairing to the bar, and to mend something.

clue.text: She shows skill in carving ham

indicators.note: skill is put inside the cut-up letters
carving cuts the word ham up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: art is skill or craft

explanation.surface: A woman displays her talent when slicing the joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is the definition, standing for any woman's name. 'carving' scrambles the letters of 'ham' and 'in' puts the skill word inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Martha is a woman's given name, so a female, standing for any woman.

clue.text: A slice of processed American cheese

indicators.note: A slice of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A slice of factory-made cheese from the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a mild Dutch cheese with a red wax rind.

clue.text: Regard sailor with horror? Not half!.

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual abbreviation for a sailor

indicators.note: not half means only half of the word horror is kept, here its first half

explanation.surface: Does one look at a seaman with dread? Not half, comes the emphatic reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', but here it keeps the first half of HORROR. The definition 'Regard ... with horror' reads through the whole clue, though the parse uses only 'Regard'.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor something is to view or consider it with loathing.

clue.text: Storm caused by parking on drive

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another means it follows it

parts.note: to drive something in hard is to ram it
P is the standard abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A tempest brought on by leaving the car on the driveway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drive' suggests a driveway but is the verb RAM.
explanation.definitionFit: To ramp is an old verb meaning to rage or rush about furiously.

clue.text: Gets ready to fight artist about manuscript

indicators.note: about here means turned about, so the letters for artist face the other way

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, is a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter turning round to a document prepares for battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns only the artist piece, which then comes before the manuscript abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To arm is to equip with weapons in preparation for combat.

clue.text: It precedes the final passion

explanation.surface: Something comes before the championship match, along with strong feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A heat is a preliminary race leading to a final; heat also means intense emotion.

clue.text: Where one waits for Ena with a motor, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters given might be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A place to wait for a woman named Ena who is bringing a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges ENA and MOTOR into the answer; 'with a' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: An anteroom is a small waiting room leading into a larger chamber.

clue.text: No-one in abandoned liner has oil distilled from orange flowers

indicators.note: the zero letter is placed inside the rearranged letters
abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained behaviour, so the letters of liner are set loose

parts.note: no one is nobody, a zero, represented by the round letter O

explanation.surface: Nobody aboard a deserted ocean liner has a fragrant citrus extract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' scrambles LINER to NERLI, and 'in' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Neroli is the essential oil from bitter-orange blossom, used in perfume.

clue.text: Music in D Sharp, nothing unusual at the end of the day

indicators.note: unusual means the letters are put in an unusual order

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: at the end of the day takes only the final letter of the word day

explanation.surface: A piece in D sharp, nothing out of the ordinary when all is said and done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges DSHARP plus O to RHAPSOD; 'at the end of' adds Y, the last letter of 'day'. 'At the end of the day' poses as the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhapsody is a free-flowing, emotional musical composition.

clue.text: Rope for the horses

explanation.surface: A line of cord meant for the horses.
explanation.definitionFit: String is thin cord, and a racing stable's string is the group of horses it trains.
